description: PRM* builds a probabilistic roadmap like PRM does, but each new node connects to the older nodes within a radius that shrinks as the graph grows: `r(n) = γ (ln n / n)^(1/d)`, where `n` counts the nodes and `d` is the dimension. The k-nearest form connects to the `⌈k ln n⌉` nearest nodes instead. If `γ` is above a bound that depends on the dimension and the free volume (or `k` above `e (1 + 1/d)`), the cost of the best path in the graph converges to the optimal cost (*asymptotic optimality*). Each node still has only about `ln n` neighbours, so the graph grows at nearly the cost of plain PRM. Use it when you query one environment many times and want paths that get better with more samples.

papers.title: Sampling-based algorithms for optimal motion planning
papers.venue: The International Journal of Robotics Research
